regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: FOLFIRI combines irinotecan with folinic-acid-modulated fluorouracil. The shared NCCP protocol covers advanced colorectal cancer, metastatic oesophageal carcinoma and second-line locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic carcinoma; the indication must therefore be confirmed before interpreting the evidence and treatment plan.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Advanced colorectal cancer; metastatic oesophageal cancer; second-line locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Irinotecan is converted to SN-38, which inhibits topoisomerase I and disrupts DNA replication. Fluorouracil impairs thymidylate synthesis and nucleic-acid function; folinic acid stabilises the fluorouracil–thymidylate-synthase complex.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Every 14 days: irinotecan and folinic acid on day 1, fluorouracil bolus followed by a 46-hour continuous infusion, continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity under the current NCCP protocol.
key_points: Shared protocol with three disease contexts
DPD status is required before fluorouracil
Delayed diarrhoea and acute cholinergic symptoms require distinct management

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Disease-control and survival-prolonging systemic therapy in advanced or metastatic gastrointestinal cancer.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm which NCCP indication applies before treatment.
The pivotal evidence record supports the metastatic colorectal-cancer backbone and does not validate every listed indication.
Confirm DPD testing before first fluorouracil exposure unless previously completed.
eligibility_orientation: Review ECOG status, blood counts, renal and hepatic function.
Assess baseline bowel frequency, chronic bowel disease, obstruction risk and ability to manage diarrhoea.
Review bilirubin and hepatic reserve because irinotecan exposure and toxicity may increase with impairment.
important_cautions: Use caution in patients with more than three loose bowel movements daily, prior pelvic/abdominal radiotherapy, older age or significant comorbidity.
UGT1A1*28 homozygosity may increase irinotecan toxicity risk; testing and starting-dose decisions remain consultant-directed.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Moderate, driven by irinotecan in the current NCCP antiemetic classification.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the protocol-linked moderate-risk antiemetic pathway.
Have atropine available for acute irinotecan cholinergic syndrome when clinically indicated.
Provide a written delayed-diarrhoea treatment and escalation plan before discharge.
patient_education: Explain the difference between acute infusion-associated cholinergic symptoms and delayed diarrhoea.
Contact the service urgently for fever, persistent diarrhoea, reduced intake, dizziness or dehydration.
Explain ambulatory pump care, disconnection and line-problem escalation.
special_support: Review hydration, electrolytes and nutritional status after significant diarrhoea.
Consider oral cryotherapy/ice chips during fluorouracil bolus where locally used and not contraindicated.

baseline: DPD phenotype and/or genotype assessment according to the current pathway.
Bowel history, cardiac history where relevant and treatment-fitness assessment.
before_each_cycle: Current and worst diarrhoea, mucositis/stomatitis and infection symptoms.
Recovery of treatment-related toxicity to the protocol-defined level before irinotecan.
priority_toxicities: Hepatic impairment and dehydration-related renal deterioration
urgent_review_signals: Persistent diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dehydration or inability to maintain intake
Chest pain or acute cardiopulmonary symptoms during fluoropyrimidine exposure
Severe mucositis or rapidly worsening performance status
Pump failure, extravasation or line complication

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Every 14 days: irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil bolus on day 1, followed by fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² over 46 hours in the encoded protocol.
route_and_duration: Irinotecan is infused intravenously, followed by folinic acid/fluorouracil according to the official sequence.
Fluorouracil includes a bolus and a continuous ambulatory infusion.
practical_workflow: Confirm indication, DPD result, bowel-toxicity history and current component dose levels.
Ensure venous access, pump availability and disconnection arrangements.
Use the official NCCP protocol for exact sequence, diluents, compatibility and dose-reduction levels.
Arrange access-device education and a named disconnection location/time; confirm written pump, spill and out-of-hours instructions.
observation_and_access: Observe for acute cholinergic symptoms and infusion reactions.
Provide direct out-of-hours access for diarrhoea, fever and pump or line complications.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Bevacizumab with an irinotecan and fluoropyrimidine backbone for metastatic colorectal cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: FOLFIRI + bevacizumab is used for cancer of the colon or rectum that has spread. Treatment aims to control the cancer; the likely benefit and review plan depend on your individual situation. Surgery may be reconsidered in selected cases after multidisciplinary review.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Metastatic carcinoma of the colon or rectum
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Irinotecan is converted to SN-38, which inhibits topoisomerase I and disrupts DNA replication. Fluorouracil impairs thymidylate synthesis and nucleic-acid function; folinic acid stabilises the fluorouracil–thymidylate-synthase complex. Bevacizumab binds VEGF-A and inhibits angiogenic signalling; effects on normal vessels and healing explain the additional vascular, renal and procedural monitoring.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Day 1: bevacizumab, irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, then a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. A cycle lasts 14 days; your team confirms the next treatment.
key_points: Metastatic colorectal indication; confirm treatment line and molecular/MDT context
Bevacizumab: blood pressure, proteinuria, bleeding/clotting, gastrointestinal perforation and wound-healing assessment

disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm metastatic colorectal indication, previous therapy and treatment goals.

eligibility_orientation: Review ECOG status, blood counts, renal and hepatic function.
Assess baseline bowel frequency, chronic bowel disease, obstruction risk and ability to manage diarrhoea.
Review bilirubin and hepatic reserve because irinotecan exposure and toxicity may increase with impairment.
important_cautions: Use caution in patients with more than three loose bowel movements daily, prior pelvic/abdominal radiotherapy, older age or significant comorbidity.
UGT1A1*28 homozygosity may increase irinotecan toxicity risk; testing and starting-dose decisions remain consultant-directed.
Assess bleeding, thromboembolic history, uncontrolled hypertension, bowel obstruction/perforation risk, fistulae and recent or planned surgery.
Coordinate port insertion or other procedures and wound healing with bevacizumab timing using the current NCCP source and consultant plan.

patient_education: Explain the difference between acute infusion-associated cholinergic symptoms and delayed diarrhoea.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Bevacizumab with an oxaliplatin and fluoropyrimidine backbone for metastatic colorectal cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Modified FOLFOX-6 + bevacizumab is used for cancer of the colon or rectum that has spread. Treatment aims to control the cancer; the likely benefit and review plan depend on your individual situation. Surgery may be reconsidered in selected cases after multidisciplinary review.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Metastatic carcinoma of the colon or rectum
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Oxaliplatin produces platinum–DNA cross-links. Fluorouracil disrupts thymidylate synthesis and nucleic-acid function, while folinic acid stabilises the fluorouracil–thymidylate-synthase complex and increases fluorouracil activity. Bevacizumab binds VEGF-A and inhibits angiogenic signalling; effects on normal vessels and healing explain the additional vascular, renal and procedural monitoring.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Day 1: bevacizumab, oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil, then a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. A cycle lasts 14 days; your team confirms the next treatment.
key_points: Metastatic colorectal indication; confirm treatment line and molecular/MDT context
Bevacizumab: blood pressure, proteinuria, bleeding/clotting, gastrointestinal perforation and wound-healing assessment

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Disease control in metastatic colorectal cancer; review potential conversion to local treatment through the MDT when relevant.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm metastatic colorectal indication, previous therapy and treatment goals.
Review the appropriate molecular work-up and alternatives in the MDT; this regimen is not a substitute for biomarker-directed treatment selection.
Confirm DPD testing before fluorouracil; review individual comorbidities and fitness.
eligibility_orientation: Review baseline blood counts, renal and hepatic function.
Assess baseline peripheral neuropathy and whether it causes functional impairment.
Confirm that pregnancy, breastfeeding and relevant hypersensitivity exclusions have been addressed.
important_cautions: Individual suitability, duration and dose decisions remain protocol- and consultant-directed.
Assess bleeding, thromboembolic history, uncontrolled hypertension, bowel obstruction/perforation risk, fistulae and recent or planned surgery.
Coordinate port insertion or other procedures and wound healing with bevacizumab timing using the current NCCP source and consultant plan.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Moderate, mapped from the oxaliplatin-containing regimen in the current NCCP antiemetic classification.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the protocol-linked moderate-risk antiemetic pathway and provide breakthrough treatment instructions.
Ensure DPD testing and fluoropyrimidine counselling are complete before first treatment.
patient_education: Explain acute cold-triggered dysaesthesia and avoidance of cold exposure after oxaliplatin.
Provide an early-contact plan for diarrhoea, stomatitis, fever, respiratory symptoms or pump/line problems.
Confirm the patient understands ambulatory infusion-pump care and the planned disconnection pathway.
Explain why urine and blood-pressure checks remain necessary without symptoms, and why all procedures must be discussed before treatment.
special_support: Review venous-access suitability for the 46-hour fluorouracil infusion.
Escalate suspected laryngopharyngeal dysaesthesia or unexplained respiratory symptoms for clinical assessment.

baseline: FBC, renal function and liver profile.
Peripheral-neuropathy assessment and relevant comorbidity review.
Blood pressure and urinalysis for protein; cardiac/vascular history, wounds and procedure plans.
before_each_cycle: Current and worst-since-last-cycle diarrhoea and stomatitis.
Treatment delay and current component dose levels when relevant.
Blood pressure and urine protein as defined by the NCCP protocol; quantify proteinuria when indicated.
Bleeding, thrombosis symptoms, abdominal symptoms, wound healing and any planned procedures.
priority_toxicities: Oxaliplatin sensory neuropathy and acute cold-related dysaesthesia
urgent_review_signals: Persistent grade 2 or greater diarrhoea, dehydration or abdominal pain
Chest or respiratory symptoms during or after treatment, including during fluorouracil infusion
Pump failure, extravasation or central-line complication
Uncontrolled bleeding, severe abdominal pain, acute neurological symptoms or suspected vascular event

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Day 1 bevacizumab and the chemotherapy backbone, including fluorouracil bolus and 2400 mg/m² over 46 hours; repeat every 14 days as prescribed. Use the exact NCCP sequence, infusion times and compatibility instructions.
route_and_duration: Oxaliplatin and folinic acid are administered intravenously on day 1.
Fluorouracil includes an intravenous bolus and a continuous 46-hour infusion.
Bevacizumab is an IV infusion. Initial/subsequent or rapid-infusion arrangements must follow the authorised local pathway.
practical_workflow: Confirm central or otherwise locally approved venous access and ambulatory-pump arrangements.
Confirm metastatic colorectal indication, previous therapy and the current treatment goal.
Use the official NCCP protocol for sequence, compatibility, infusion duration and dose levels.
Arrange access-device education and a named disconnection location/time; confirm written pump, spill and out-of-hours instructions.
observation_and_access: Follow local observation and hypersensitivity procedures for oxaliplatin.
Ensure a documented pump-disconnection and out-of-hours contact plan.

evidence_audit.status: Source-linked focused review; independent validation pending
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: NO16966 randomised 1,401 patients with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer to FOLFOX4 or XELOX, with bevacizumab or placebo. The results below pool the chemotherapy backbones.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: This release presents the specific comparative trial below and declares its limits; it is not a systematic review.
remaining_uncertainties: The progression-free survival difference was statistically significant. Overall survival was 21.3 versus 19.9 months and did not meet statistical significance. A median is a group midpoint, not a personal deadline. These results are not an exact estimate for modified FOLFOX-6 or for adjuvant treatment.

evidence_records.publication_title: Initial therapy with FOLFOXIRI and bevacizumab for metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence_records.trial_population: TRIBE randomised 508 previously untreated patients with metastatic colorectal cancer to FOLFIRI + bevacizumab or the more intensive FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Direct FOLFIRI + bevacizumab comparator-arm evidence; does not isolate the effect of adding bevacizumab.
key_findings: Tumour response: 53% with FOLFIRI + bevacizumab versus 65% with FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab.
The more intensive triplet improved progression-free survival but caused more selected toxicities.
evidence_records.limitations: The triplet produced more responses but more important toxicities. Both groups received bevacizumab: this comparison does not measure the benefit of adding bevacizumab to FOLFIRI. These are selected trial patients, not an individual forecast or a reason to change treatment yourself.

evidence_records.publication_title: Bevacizumab in combination with oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy as first-line therapy in metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence_records.trial_population: NO16966 randomised 1,401 patients with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer to FOLFOX4 or XELOX, with bevacizumab or placebo. The results below pool the chemotherapy backbones.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: First-line treatment-family evidence; pooled FOLFOX4/XELOX backbones differ from mFOLFOX6.
key_findings: Median PFS: 9.4 versus 8.0 months; HR 0.83 (97.5% CI 0.72–0.95), P=0.0023.
Median overall survival: 21.3 versus 19.9 months; the difference was not statistically significant.
evidence_records.limitations: The progression-free survival difference was statistically significant. Overall survival was 21.3 versus 19.9 months and did not meet statistical significance. A median is a group midpoint, not a personal deadline. These results are not an exact estimate for modified FOLFOX-6 or for adjuvant treatment.
